narrative.overview:
The weekly brief is the week's weather report for a startup: the condition is the sky, and how to proceed follows from it. The homepage opens on a sky tinted by the week's condition, full width, with the guidance written on it and the two scores on a panel of paper; a storm week and a sunny week look like different pages. Beneath the sky the brief is filed on cool paper in a blue-black ink, read top to bottom: the five areas, the trust facts, then the sections that explain them. The record band under the navigation of every route is every month-end reading since January 2012, drawn as the same four conditions.

The world borrows a modern weather app's glanceability and an investor update's restraint: the condition drives the page, structure stays quiet, every engraved line on the band is drawn from data, and nothing decorative is added except the sky's slow clouds. It refuses the dark data panel with glowing accents, the credit-agreement document Covenant was, and the editorial broadsheet. "Forecast" names the world for contributors; it never appears in reader copy beyond the weather words the site already uses.

Light is the identity; dark is the second theme, the same page at night: the paper goes blue-black and each sky darkens to its condition after dark. With no stored choice the device setting picks the theme, and a stored choice wins (`app/layout.tsx`, the theme bootstrap). With scripts off, the stylesheet's base draws, which is the dark `:root` block.

The direction contract is `.impeccable/surfaces/app-page-tsx.md`.
keyCharacteristics: Colour commits at page scale in two places: the record band, and the homepage's sky. Everything else is ink on paper.
Two voices: Bricolage Grotesque binds, Source Sans 3 explains.
Ruled lists and lifted sheets: hairlines and a 2px ink rule over a list; a card or a button carries a layered three-step shadow, and nothing nested repeats it.
Every drawing puts the easier side up or to the right.
A quiet week moves only the sky's clouds, and they hold still under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Two Meanings Rule
rules.body: A hue on the page is a condition or a crossed line. Anything else is ink. A caveat (cached sources, a scoring note, an archived week, guidance held back) is ink with an outlined diamond, never red: shape carries the state where hue cannot.

rules.name: The Ink Is the Action Rule
rules.body: Links, buttons, focus rings, the selected pill and the caret are the ink in every week. A condition's colour means the condition and nothing else.

rules.name: The Two Fields Rule
rules.body: Colour commits at page scale in two places: the record band on every route, and the sky on the homepage's first screen. Both draw the four conditions and nothing else. The regime atmosphere wash is off everywhere else (`--atmosphere-*: transparent`), so the paper below the sky, and every other route, stays paper.

rules.name: The Binding Voice Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque sets what the page commits to: the guidance, the condition word, area names, score figures, headings and the wordmark. Source Sans 3 sets everything that explains. The voice reaches the page through real rules only (`:where(h1, h2)`, `.type-section`, `.text-display`, `.type-stamp`, `.type-figure`); there is no `font-display` utility.

rules.name: The Type Step Rule
rules.body: Every step is at least 1.125x the one below it at both ends of the range (`tests/typeSteps.test.tsx`). Two sizes closer than that read as one job set twice.

rules.name: The One Number, One Face Rule
rules.body: A figure in a sentence or beside its label stays in its voice with `tabular-nums`. Mono is for a column, a before/after pair or a rail's own labels. A figure that appears on more than one surface is the same figure everywhere.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose stops at 60ch, about 69 characters in Source Sans 3, from a base-layer rule on `p` and on list items holding text; a utility on the element overrides it, and a flex or grid row is exempt.

rules.name: The Say-It-Once Rule
rules.body: Depth is said once per stack: the outermost sheet lifts, everything in it is flat. A card inside a card is still wrong, shadow or not. Covenant's Flat Paper Rule (no surface casts a shadow, 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-12) is retired.

dos: Do name a condition with `data-regime` and read `--regime-accent` or `--regime-ink`; never type a condition hex at the call site.
Do print a condition word through `ConditionWord` or `ConditionLabel`, never as a bare label in the surrounding ink.
Do draw links, buttons and focus rings in the ink, with links underlined.
Do set the guidance, condition word, area names, score figures, headings and wordmark in Bricolage Grotesque, and everything that explains in Source Sans 3.
Do lift the outermost sheet with `--elev-card` and a button with `--elev-control`, and separate lists with a 2px ink rule over hairline rows.
Do read a sky from its tokens (`--regime-sky-*`) and give anything on it the sky's ink.
Do give every condition a pattern as well as a fill wherever it fills an area, so the drawing survives greyscale and colour-vision deficiency.
Do label each line and tick where it sits, and keep the easier side up or to the right.
Do keep red for a crossed line, always with a glyph and a word.
Do keep the record band's two records apart: fields are month-end readings scored today; marks are briefs as published.
donts: Don't put a card inside a card, or a shadow on anything nested in a lifted sheet.
Don't draw a zero-offset shadow or a glow.
Don't use a condition's colour for a control or a section label, or wash a page in it outside the homepage's sky.
Don't add a hue that is neither a condition nor a crossed line; a caveat is ink with a diamond.
Don't add a legend where a label in place will do.
Don't add a decorative mark the record did not draw.
Don't set Chivo Mono for a figure that does not align with another.
Don't set a word under 12px, set italics, or type capitals outside a badge.
Don't hand-pick a z-index that can meet a global layer.
